correctness.rationale: If E is not coordinatewise ell_1, density of finite-support vectors and unconditionality produce a positive finite-support unit vector a with sum_i a_i>1. Its positive norming f has each f(e_i)<=1; f(a)=1 forces f(e_i)<1 on some positive coefficient. Flipping all other signs and adjoining a dual scalar coordinate of value 1 produces norm-one x,F with F(x)=1 but F^+(x^+)=a_i f(e_i)<a_i=||F^+|| ||x^+||, so HNAp fails. If E=ell_1, X is ell_1 over the enlarged index set; equality in the coordinatewise dual Holder inequality forces F_k=sgn(x_k) for every nonzero x_k, giving both Jordan-part norming identities. This reconstructs all quantifiers including finite/countable E, zero positive parts and the dual norm.
risks: The use of a Schauder basis, not merely an abstract unconditional coordinate set, ensures that finite-support norms determine the completion and dual functionals are determined by coordinates.
The exact-rational examples verify selected witnesses only; the analytic theorem is independent of finite enumeration.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural stability classification: adding a single scalar ell_1 coordinate preserves the source-defined hereditary norm-attaining property exactly for atomic AL norms, across every finite dimension and all countable normalized 1-unconditional Schauder bases. It strengthens the motivating 3D isolated counterexample into a clean iff theorem, shows that even Euclidean/Hilbert and square planes lose HNAp under this extension, and identifies norm additivity on positive disjoint coordinates as the governing structural invariant. It is not a routine recomputation or an arbitrary restricted parameter.
risks: The classification depends on the added scalar summand having the outer ell_1 norm; arbitrary absolute direct sums are not covered.
